newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus devalues rouble with new currency range.
newsitem.headline: Belarus devalues rouble with new currency range.

text.p: Belarus devalued its rouble on Thursday by introducing a new floating corridor of 15,500-21,000 units per U.S. dollar, replacing the old range of 11,300-15,500, a senior central bank official said.
Vladimir Luzgin, director of the National Bank's hard currency department, told Reuters officials had not decided how long the new corridor would be in effect.
"The period of the new hard currency corridor has not been specified, but it will be done so in accordance with the financial policies of the Russian Federation," he said. He did not elaborate.

Belarus, where reforms have ground to a halt, conducts over half of its foreign trade with neighbouring Russia. Russia has set a new currency corridor for its rouble running until the end of this year.
Minsk's International Currency Exchange, where enterprises are required to sell 50 percent of their hard currency earnings for Belarussian roubles, had enforced the old corridor.
The Belarussian rouble slipped to 16,300 per dollar on Thursday on the exchange from 16,100 the previous day.
On the interbank market, where the corridor is not in effect, the Belarussian rouble traded at 25,000-27,000 per dollar.
Some central bank officials criticised the level of the new corridor, saying it had not devalued the rouble sufficiently.
Belarus' maverick president, Alexander Lukashenko, who has taken a go-slow approach to reform, said in September 1996 he did not support hard currency corridors, used as an inflation-busting measure.
Last year, the International Monetary Fund froze most of a $300 million standby credit and the World Bank halted its credits over concerns about the pace of reform in the former Soviet republic.
The old currency range was launched in July 1996 and expired at the end of last year.
